full_text:
Cyclone Akvan was crawling north-northwestwards over the central parts of the South Bay of Bengal and the adjoining west-central Bay at 0830 hrs IST on Tuesday, November 17. Per the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Akvan will become a Severe Cyclone tonight. Per the latest IMD update at 0530 hrs IST, the storm was 610 km east of Chennai, 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam. The IMD expects it to turn Very Severe on the evening of November 19 and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts around noon on November 20.
Cyclone Akvan: Etymology
Akvan began as a well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal on November 14. Andhra Pradesh has already been through Cyclone Arnab in late October and Cyclone Murasu this month. The name Akvan was suggested by Iran, which refers to Akvan-e Div, a demon in the Persian epic Shahnameh. It means 'evil mind.'
Cyclone Akvan: Landfall & Rainfall
Reports on the IMD bulletin say winds could reach 130 kmph, and an orange alert is out for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. A storm surge of 1 to 1.5 meters could flood low-lying coastal Andhra at landfall. Coastal Andhra may get heavy to very heavy rain on November 19 and 20, with isolated extremely heavy falls. Those could cross 20 cm.
Odisha is likely to see heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places from November 19 to 21. Chennai, Tiruvallur and Chengalpattu get heavy rain from November 17. North Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal could see heavy to very heavy rain on November 18 and 19. No direct landfall is expected over Tamil Nadu.

Cyclone Akvan: Evacuation Ops
Odisha deployed 74 rescue teams on Monday and began early evacuation in its southern districts, per PTI . Fishermen off north Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have been told to stay off the sea, and boats already out must return immediately.
